name: Edwards's Pheasant
rangeDescription: Lowlands of central vietnam (on verge of extinction in wild)
description: Critically endangered species with tiny populations in remote hilly terrain of central Vietnam, where it inhabits densely vegetated hillsides with dense low cover. There are no recent reports of the species in the wild.

name: Sri Lanka Drongo
rangeDescription: Western sri lanka
description: Large, upright, blackish bird with a long, deeply-forked tail and tuft of feathers on the forehead. Typically found in pairs, often in mixed flocks, within the understory of humid forests in the lowlands and foothills of Sri Lanka’s Wet Zone.

name: Huambo Cisticola
rangeDescription: West-central angola
description: Large, plain, long-tailed cisticola with a rufous cap, gray-brown back, and pale whitish underparts. Found in open habitats with grass and small trees, often in rugged and mountainous areas.

name: Dimorphic Jewel-babbler
rangeDescription: Eastern new guinea (huon gulf to collingwood bay)
description: A medium-sized, long-tailed, ground-dwelling bird of lowland and foothill forest. White throat and upper chest, bordered by a thin black line across the chest and a broad black band through the eye.

name: Akohekohe
rangeDescription: Ohia forest of eastern maui; formerly on molokai
description: A large, rare Hawaiian Honeycreeper of high elevation wet forests on eastern Maui. Its bushy, forward-pointing crest is distinctive.

name: Abyssinian Ground-Hornbill
rangeDescription: Senegambia to ethiopia, northern uganda, and northeastern kenya
description: A huge ground-dwelling hornbill. Males have a mix of blue and red bare facial skin, while females have entirely blue facial skin.

name: Rufous Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Alaska to northwestern usa; winters to southern mexico
description: Adult males are almost entirely orange with bright white chest and some green on the back (can be solid green like Allen's Hummingbird). Throat is iridescent, and depending on the light, can look anywhere from red to orange to yellow to lime green.

name: Rufous-sided Scrub-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Southern suriname and eastern brazil to northeastern bolivia and northeastern paraguay
description: Tiny flycatcher with a long tail. Note the white throat contrasting with the brown back, yellowish belly, and cinnamon flanks.

name: Black-billed Gull
rangeDescription: South island (new zealand); winters to north island
description: Pale gull endemic to New Zealand. White with light gray wings and back.

name: Saddle-billed Stork
rangeDescription: Locally in sub-saharan africa
description: A tall, lanky, black-and-white stork with a unique red, yellow, and black bill. The male has dark-brown eyes, and the female has yellow eyes.

name: Crozet Shag
rangeDescription: Prince edward, marion, and crozet islands
description: Learn about Imperial Cormorant (Crozet): explore photos, sounds, and observations collected by birders around the world.

name: Rust-and-yellow Tanager
rangeDescription: Andes of southeastern peru to bolivia and northwestern argentina
description: Small, bright yellow tanager of middle and high elevations. Males have a rusty orange head, while females have only a hint of rusty color, and immatures are plain yellow.

name: Brown Oriole
rangeDescription: New guinea, including raja ampat islands (off western new guinea)
description: A brown oriole with a darker head and cheeks, a dull orange bill, and extensively streaked pale underparts. Juveniles show a pale eyebrow and dark bill.

name: Bornean Stubtail
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern borneo (kinabalu to liang kubung)
description: Minute, ground-dwelling warbler of Borneo’s central mountain ranges. Scurries about like a rodent in the undergrowth, where it can be difficult to see well; note bright orangish brow stripe, brown back, and gray sides.

name: Yellow-rumped Munia
rangeDescription: Northern australia (cambridge gulf, western australia to arnhem land)
description: Small finchlike bird with brown wings, pale bill, and yellowish rump. Found in areas with tall grass, often in flocks beside rivers or floodplains, sometimes mixed with other seed-eating species.

name: Tahiti Monarch
rangeDescription: Highlands of tahiti (society islands)
description: A distinctive large glossy-black flycatcher with a pale bluish-ivory bill. Female has a cinnamon head, a buffy chest, white underparts and brown upperparts.

name: Short-bearded Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Western new guinea (mount wilhelmina in snow mountains)
description: A long, slender honeyeater of subalpine forest and shrubland in western New Guinea. All sooty gray-black plumage with a long tail and a fairly long, curved bill, 2 white tufts emanating from the base of the bill, and a yellow-orange wattle at the back of the eye.

name: Lovely Cotinga
rangeDescription: Gulf lowlands of southern mexico (veracruz) to southeastern costa rica
description: Unobtrusive, rather chunky bird of forest canopy in tropical forest of humid lowlands. Most often seen as a single male perched on exposed high branches, less often at fruiting trees where can be quite low.

name: Burmese Nuthatch
rangeDescription: Myanmar to southeastern yunnan, thailand, laos, cambodia, and southern vietnam
description: Gray with a slender black mask and warm underparts. Male has white extending from the throat onto the cheeks, and averages darker below than the female, which also lacks the male’s white cheek patch.

name: Rufous-vented Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Eastern bhutan to northeastern india, northern myanmar, and northern laos
description: A large laughingthrush with a heavy black bill. Note black mask on face, yellow throat, and reddish belly.
